holidays.name: Boy Scouts Day
holidays.description: A day honoring the founding of the Boy Scouts of America, celebrated with knot-tying, campfire stories, and a fresh round of 'be prepared' energy.
holidays.origin: The Boy Scouts of America was incorporated on February 8, 1910, by William D. Boyce, a Chicago publisher, after the Scouting movement began in Britain.
holidays.funFact: Boyce reportedly got the idea after a London fog-bound encounter with a Scout who helped him find his way and refused a tip.

holidays.name: Kite Flying Day
holidays.description: A day to take a kite outside and let the wind do the work. Ideal for anyone who wants to feel like a kid again or lose a kite in a tree.
holidays.origin: An informal, unofficial observance that grew out of kite enthusiast communities and the generally breezy weather of late winter in many regions.
holidays.funFact: Kites have been flown in China for over 2,000 years, and early ones were used to measure distances and send military signals.

holidays.name: Molasses Bread Day
holidays.description: A celebration of dark, sticky, slightly bitter baked goodness. Slather it with butter and pretend you live on a 1700s farmstead.
holidays.origin: A food observance that celebrates molasses bread, a staple of colonial American kitchens when molasses was cheaper and more available than refined sugar.
holidays.funFact: Molasses was so central to colonial trade that the Molasses Act of 1733 taxed imports and helped stoke tensions leading to the American Revolution.

holidays.name: Safer Internet Day
holidays.description: A global day for promoting safer and more responsible use of technology, especially among kids. It is a good excuse to finally change that password that is just your pet's name.
holidays.origin: It began in 2004 as an initiative of the EU SafeBorders project and was taken up by the Insafe network. It is now celebrated in well over 100 countries, typically on the second Tuesday of February.
holidays.funFact: It is a movable observance, so it only falls on February 8 in some years, such as 2022 and 2028.

holidays.name: Just Because Day
holidays.description: A day to do something nice, silly, or random for absolutely no reason. No explanation or occasion required.
holidays.origin: Greeting card companies and online holiday lists popularized this occasion as a catch-all celebration, giving people permission to send gifts or compliments without a motive.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'just because' is so flexible that it works as a full answer to the question 'why?' in nearly every English conversation.
